correctness.rationale: Explicit F/L definitions and cubic triple-angle identities reduce 2m-term sums to four template families. Their fourth-order integer recurrence has unit constant coefficient, so four shifts determine the infinite GCD. Direct integer-linear evaluations give the exact two 2*gcd(.,30) formulas, and Fibonacci/Lucas modular periods simplify them to the boxed half-length indicators. The actual accompanying verify.py was executed successfully for all m<=80 and n<=7, including negative-index template values. The universal argument uses the stated recurrences and congruences, not finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: A published number-theory problem explicitly asks for the GCD of consecutive cubic Fibonacci/Lucas sums. This yields complete exact answers for both sequences at every even window, distinguishing parity and divisibility of the half-length with sharp 2-, 3-, 5-factors. The family is natural and infinite and its uniform structure corrects a displayed conjectural specialization. The odd-window/general-Gibonacci cases remain open here; no broader accomplishment is claimed.
